title: Beyond the scales: Marine archaeogenomics for the conservation and restoration of fisheries.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Crossref and Europe PMC records (type = Review, Science 393:472-479, subscription-only, no PubMed Central copy, hasSuppl = N, hasData = N, no linked data banks); two guessed Science supplementary URLs both returned HTTP 403; Zenodo and Dryad searches returned 0 records. I then went to the third-party sequence archives the reviewed studies used and counted entries: European Nucleotide Archive project PRJEB52865 (ancient Atlantic cod) has 37 sequencing runs, PRJEB52723 (ancient Baltic herring) has 162 runs.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Only the abstract was readable. The claim that the review compiles ancient DNA (aDNA, degraded DNA recovered from old bones) studies of archaeological fish remains from 2020-2025 comes from the abstract alone; I could not see any table of those studies, because the full text is paywalled and no supplement is listed.

a1_downloadable.note: FAIL. The paper is a paywalled Science Review with no open full text, no supplementary files listed by Europe PMC (hasSuppl = N), no linked data repository, and no Zenodo or Dryad deposit. Both attempted supplementary file URLs returned HTTP 403. There is no dataset attached to this paper to download.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: FAIL (assessed, not reached as the first killer). A review publishes no table of features and labels. Any target - e.g. which fish population an archaeological bone came from - would have to be built from scratch by re-processing dozens of other groups' raw sequencing files.

a3_inputs_present.note: FAIL. The inputs exist only as raw short-read sequencing files in the European Nucleotide Archive, referenced by accession, and would need alignment and genotype-likelihood calling before any model could see them. Project instructions forbid downloading raw sequencing data.

a4_units_stated.note: Not applicable - no measurement table exists, so there are no units to state.

a5_enough_rows.note: FAIL. The unit is one archaeological fish specimen. I counted 37 sequencing runs in PRJEB52865 (ancient cod) and 162 in PRJEB52723 (ancient Baltic herring, ~40 specimens); published aDNA fish studies report tens of specimens each, so the whole 2020-2025 literature is low hundreds - far under the ~1,500-row bar.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: unknown; raw whole-genome short reads, hundreds of GB to TB across the reviewed projects
a6_fits_laptop.note: FAIL. Turning raw ancient-DNA reads into a feature table means alignment and variant calling across whole fish genomes - well beyond a 16 GB CPU-only laptop and beyond the 50 MB download rule.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Cannot be checked. The paper states no counts I can read (abstract only), and there is no download to compare against.

a8_label_provenance.note: Not assessable. With no label column there is nothing to trace, though note the natural target in this field - the population a specimen is assigned to - is itself the output of a mixed-stock assignment model, which would be a circularity problem if anyone tried.

honest_claim_h3: No claim is possible: this is a literature review with no dataset of its own.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use ancient fish bone DNA to predict which wild population and ocean region each archaeological specimen came from.
plain_idea.train_on: The project I considered would train on low-coverage whole-genome sequence from archaeological fish bones, labelled with the reference population the specimen was assigned to. Verified count: 37 sequencing runs for ancient cod and 162 for ancient Baltic herring, i.e. tens of specimens per study.
plain_idea.predict: Which modern reference population (spawning stock and region) a bone belongs to. The true answer comes from genotyping modern reference fish of known origin and running a statistical assignment test on the ancient sample.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Fisheries managers set recovery targets from recent decades of catch records; knowing which stocks people actually caught 1,000 years ago would move those baselines. But the labels themselves come from an assignment model, so a predictor would be learning that model, not biology.

ml_idea: Considered and rejected: assign archaeological fish bones to source populations from low-coverage ancient genomes. The review itself contributes no data; the underlying material is tens of specimens per study held as raw sequencing reads in the European Nucleotide Archive, and the obvious label is another model's output.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated - no dataset exists to process. Building one would require aligning raw ancient-DNA reads from several third-party projects, which is a bioinformatics pipeline, not a laptop modelling job.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Ask Europe PMC whether the paper has any supplementary files or linked data banks. It answered no on both in one call, which killed the project in under a minute.

verdict_reason: Paywalled Science Review with zero attached data: no supplement, no repository deposit, nothing to open. Fails A1 outright, and the third-party ancient-DNA studies it summarises hold only tens of specimens each (37 and 162 sequencing runs in the two projects I checked) as raw whole-genome reads, so A3, A5 and A6 fail too. Review articles are a systematic dead end for this pipeline unless they ship a compiled table.
